protocol: Official April 8-21 train and April 22-28 validation split; no random-log or hidden-test outcomes; causal exposure histories contain only strictly earlier item, clock, duration, and tab tokens; four user-ID-modulo folds for residual selection.

experiments.name: current-session causal exposure Transformer
experiments.architecture: Full-metadata pointwise DeepFM plus one-layer, four-head causal exposure-history Transformer; length 10, width 32, watch-ratio auxiliary weight 0.4.
experiments.evidence: Only 18.15% of validation rows had a prior impression in the same 30-minute session. Epoch 4 reached 0.60735643 standalone (0.67531669 GAUC, 0.53939617 nDCG@5), but every global residual fold selected zero weight. Timestamp-only history gates produced a best fixed 0.61280996 on depth >=5 rows, but held-out fold 0 regressed; the candidate was not promoted.

experiments.name: full-user causal exposure Transformer
experiments.architecture: The same Transformer without the 30-minute reset, retaining the most recent 10 exposures per user.
experiments.evidence: Coverage increased to 99.66% of validation rows and mean history length to 9.70, but epoch 2 reached only 0.60686481 standalone (0.67473698 GAUC, 0.53899270 nDCG@5). Its residual OOF primary regressed to 0.61279380 and its fixed result regressed to 0.61279500, with two negative held-out folds.

successful_tracked_run_totals.note: The lightweight timestamp-gate feature builder did not emit its own tracker record and is excluded; both model trainers and all metric audits are included.

conclusion: Causal self-attention over outcome-free exposure history did not add information beyond the existing pointwise, aggregate-history, and slate corrections. Session history was too sparse, while nearly complete full-user history was less accurate and regressed the ensemble. The 0.6128046513 champion remains authoritative.
